calls.title: ShiftKey + GrowthBook
calls.summary: The team agreed to shift from weekly to biweekly or monthly meetings, as proposed by Chris Sanders, citing steady progress and limited agenda items. Tyler Reber supported this by noting the absence of pressing content, while Clark Finley requested the cancellation of the recurring meeting series. They decided to primarily rely on their Slack channel for updates and quick questions to maintain communication without formal meetings. With only one feature flag set in use, deeper performance reviews are unnecessary for now, and any plans to expand monitoring capabilities will be deferred to future phases. This approach fosters operational flexibility and prioritizes responsiveness, with team members expressing comfort in reducing regular calls but remaining open to reschedule as new issues arise.

calls.summary: The meeting detailed the successful completion of the migration from LaunchDarkly to Growth Book, achieving feature parity and transitioning to production calls with no client complaints. Currently, the team is utilizing only feature flags for controlling segmentation and rollout status, with ongoing logging managed through Grafana due to time constraints. Chris Sanders emphasized the importance of a cultural shift towards data-driven development, leveraging analytics for targeted feature rollouts and enhanced user engagement.

calls.title: ShiftKey + GrowthBook
calls.summary: The team agreed on a 30% discount for a partnership, reducing the platform fee to $100k annually and unit price to $1,000. Payment terms were negotiated to allow annual upfront payments without automatic increases over 3% at renewal. The Enterprise plan was confirmed as the best fit for Shift Key, featuring crucial security and governance tools. Cost-saving data pipeline optimizations were also highlighted, potentially reducing warehouse costs by up to 90%. Tailored onboarding support and 24/7 assistance are included to facilitate integration, while urgency in closing before quarter-end was emphasized to secure discounts and marketing advantages.

calls.title: ShiftKey + GrowthBook
calls.summary: During the meeting, ShiftKey and GrowthBook discussed partnership terms, emphasizing the need to align ShiftKey's budget of $100,000 annually with GrowthBook's proposal of $187,000 over three years. Key points included ShiftKey's preference for a one-year term due to market volatility and internal policies, while GrowthBook was open to this arrangement and proposed a pricing model featuring a steep discount in the first year with gradual increases. Security requirements were also highlighted, with ShiftKey needing SOC2 reports for security approval, which GrowthBook agreed to provide. The expected user seat allocation of 50 was confirmed to meet current operational needs, and a quick follow-up call was planned to finalize details, targeting contract signing by the end of April.

calls.title: ShiftKey + GrowthBook
calls.summary: The team outlined a phased migration strategy from LaunchDarkly to GrowthBook, emphasizing dual system operation to mitigate risks. Key engineers will review current production feature flags to identify deprecated ones before migration, and the importance of cleaning up unused flags was highlighted to simplify the scope. Their environment setup aligns well with GrowthBook's model, though potential complexities arise from feature flag duplication across SDKs. Gradual migration is crucial, with plans to obtain an enterprise license key soon to facilitate testing. Shift Key primarily utilizes customer and community-level targeting, avoiding complex user-ID lists, while acknowledging risks like multiple environments and duplicate flags. The GrowthBook team’s support and a focus on verification during migration were also discussed.
calls.keywords: Feature Flags, Migration, LaunchDarkly, GrowthBook, Targeting, SDK Environments
